options.reasons: It acts on the chip you see, which is the owner's instinct, but nothing on screen shows the gesture. Headless Chromium does deliver contextmenu to the page (MEASURED), but that says nothing about the app. Escape never reaches a panel, so the menu can only close on an outside click or a pick, and clicks on the app's chrome send nothing, so it can stay open. options.reasons: The idea is right: pick with visuals on this key, which also previews the theme on the physical key, then promote it from the theme line. As written it is underspecified. options.risks: If the promote leaves the key pinned, the key stops following later shared changes after a person only meant to change the shared theme. If focus goes to Change after the press, a held Enter runs on into Change and scrolls the band away (MEASURED in the prototype).

Do not change the chips, their order or names, the Default chip's dashed frame and link mark, the radiogroup's single Tab stop, or the folded row.

Do not move focus to Change (or leave it on the now-hidden link) after Make shared; a held Enter must not reach Change.
Do not write the key's setting before the global one, and do not let the line show the old shared theme between the press and the plugin's payload.
Do not write anything on open, fold, hover, focus or Tab, and store no UI state in key settings or globals.

options.reasons: This follows the pattern of setting something on one item, then promoting it to the default. Figma has push changes to main component, Finder has Use as Defaults and Word has Set As Default. The pick is a cheap, local try-on: this key redraws in Ember and the header face shows it. Only then does one named press change every key set to Default. The link appears only in the state where it applies (an explicit known pick that differs from the shared theme). It takes the slot Change already holds unseen in that state, so one slot always holds the shared-theme action that fits: Change while the key follows, Make shared while it has its own pick. The words map onto the theme line: 'Ember (set on this key)' plus Make shared becomes 'Default (shared: Ember)'. Two steps, all in view, visuals throughout, reversible in two presses, no mode and no hidden gesture. Prototyped in a copy: 28 of 28 simulated checks pass, and nothing moves between states.
options.risks: (1) It writes two things: the global theme, then this key's theme set to "". The visible words name only 'shared', so the owner's rule 'an edit changes only what it names' is met through the result line, the title and the announcement, not the label alone. This is the owner's call; see the recommendation summary. (2) The only way to find it is by picking a chip. A person on Default who wants a new shared theme must pick first. The docs need one line. (3) At 300 to 307 px the longest line ('Default (shared: Ultraviolet)') wraps to two lines (+18.8 px), because the reserved slot grows from 68 to 86 px. Standard zoom steps from 373 (339, 298) and the 315 scrollbar case are unaffected (MEASURED). (4) Changing the shared theme from a key with its own pick that must stay (say Paper) takes three presses.

options.reasons: It answers the literal complaint (the select has no colors), keeps Change unchanged and adds no new gesture. Picking the shared theme would show colors wherever it happens.
options.risks: It adds a second gallery of look-alike chips with a different scope on one page, which invites 'which one did I press?' errors. It costs about 70 px in Advanced and breaks the Theme / Text color row pair. Steps do not drop (Change, scroll, pick), and there is no try-on: every arrow press on a radiogroup writes the global setting and redraws every key. With B in place it is redundant. Keep it as a later option only if the owner still wants colors at Change's destination.

options.reasons: A lighter answer for people who arrive through Change: the Shared defaults Theme select gets the folded band's 24 px mini chip beside it, showing the selected shared theme in its own colors. Display only, no second gallery.
options.risks: It shows only the current value, not the choices, so the popup list still has no colors. It adds an element to a paired row. Optional; not part of the recommendation.

options.reasons: The entry is visible (Change), and the colors stay in place in the band.
options.risks: It is a temporary mode: the same eight chips change meaning and blast radius. Escape never reaches a panel, so leaving needs a visible Done, and a person who forgets they are in shared mode rewrites every key with each press or arrow. The Default chip has to vanish or be disabled, which reflows the grid or leaves a dead chip. The radiogroup's label and checked state switch under assistive tech. Folding the band or selecting another key mid-mode has to be defined. It has many more states than B for the same outcome.

options.reasons: The scope is always visible, and scope switches are a known pattern (for example VS Code's User and Workspace settings tabs).
options.risks: It is a permanent mode switch on a high blast-radius control: with All selected, every chip press and arrow press rewrites the shared theme on every deck. It adds a row to the densest band, and Default means nothing in All mode. Panel storage is per panel, so the switch resets on every key selection: safer, but a user trying several keys has to set it each time. There are two kinds of checked state to explain.

options.reasons: Right click fits the owner's hint, and 'Set as default' in a context menu is a familiar Windows pattern.
options.risks: Nobody knows whether contextmenu reaches a panel in the app, and it may show the app's own menu. There is no visible affordance, so it is found only by accident. Escape never reaches a panel and app-chrome clicks send nothing, so a custom menu can stay open. It is a one-step global write with no try-on, and a stray right click redraws every Default key. It needs a menu widget with focus management. Long press does not apply to a desktop app. At best it could later be an extra shortcut to B, never the only path.

options.reasons: The shared theme is rarely changed and has a large blast radius, so a deeper route is defensible.
options.risks: It ignores the owner's explicit request and keeps the only route a colorless select two levels into Advanced.

recommendation.summary: Build B as 'Make shared', and change nothing else. When a key or dial has its own known theme that differs from the shared one, the theme line's right-hand slot (where Change sits, unseen, today) shows a link, Make shared. Pressing it makes that theme the shared theme, then sets this key back to Default so it follows. The line turns from 'Ember (set on this key)' into 'Default (shared: Ember)', the Default chip is checked and drawn in Ember, and Change returns to the slot. The shared theme is chosen from the gallery with colors, after a try-on on this key. Change and the Shared defaults select stay exactly as they are. No right click, no confirmation, no scope switch, no second gallery. The owner has one call to make: whether Make shared also sets this key to Default. I recommend it does. If it wrote only the global theme, the key would stay pinned, the line would not change, the link would just vanish, and later shared changes would skip this key. That is less feedback and a hidden trap.

options.reasons: The link appears where the person already is: they just picked a theme with the gallery, and they are looking at the result on their key. A first-time user who wants every key in Ember usually picks Ember on the first key. B puts the shared route in front of them right then, in the Change slot, which is held empty on an explicit pick today (READ pi-common.js renderThemeLine). The vocabulary lines up: the Default line says "(shared: Void)" and the explicit line says "(set on this key)". A person reading "Ember (set on this key) Make shared" can predict that the link moves Ember from "set on this key" to shared. After the press the line reads "Default (shared: Ember)", which confirms that prediction in the same words. It needs no mode, no hidden gesture and no new setting. The key's face does not change, and every Default key changes on the deck, so the panel and the deck both show the result. Formative test: T1 on a Default key, "make every key that follows the shared theme use Ember"; T2 on a key pinned to Ember, "keep this key Ember and make the others match"; T3, a probe: "if the shared theme later becomes Forest, what will this key do?"; T4: "undo that". Success: the final global theme and key theme are right, with no stray pinned key. recommendation.summary: Build D: keep Change, and turn Advanced > Shared defaults > Theme into the same named chip gallery (the seven presets, no Default chip). It is a radio group that writes only the global theme. Change lands on its checked chip. No right click, no promote link, no scope switch or mode, no confirmation. recommendation.copy: Visible label stays "Theme" in Shared defaults, so the docs path "Advanced > Shared defaults > Theme" stays true. Group accessible name: "Shared theme". Chip faces show the theme name ("Void", "Graphite", "Ultraviolet", "Midnight", "Forest", "Ember", "Paper"); chip accessible names are "Void shared theme" through "Paper shared theme". Unknown stored value, help line (two sentences, the drawn theme from resolvedDeckId()): This version does not know the stored theme "neon". Keys and dials set to Default draw Void until you pick one. Change is unchanged: visible word "Change", accessible name "Change the shared theme". No new live announcements; the radio's checked state is spoken. Never write "Use for all" or "all keys" on a control, because keys and dials with their own theme keep it. No em dashes anywhere; run node scripts/validate-release-copy.mjs after the HTML edit.
recommendation.keyboard_and_at: APG radio group, one Tab stop on the checked chip (on Void when the stored value is unknown). Right and Down move to the next chip and pick; Left and Up move to the previous one; both wrap. Home and End go to the first and last. Space or Enter on the focused chip picks it. A keydown with ev.repeat === true is ignored (preventDefault, no move, no write), so one press makes one pick: without this, a held arrow wrote 21 deck-wide themes per hold (MEASURED). Focus stays on the chip across re-renders (the same focus-keeping rebuild the band uses). The focus ring sits outside the checked ring (outline-offset 3px, the band's rule). Change moves focus to the checked chip, so a screen reader hears the group "Shared theme", then e.g. "Void shared theme, radio button, checked, 1 of 7". The band group keeps its name "Theme" and its chips keep "<Name> theme for this key" (or "dial"), so the two groups never share a name. A right click on any chip does nothing (no menu, no write). The shell's armed-button repeat guard is untouched, and clicking a shared chip while Replace shared settings is armed disarms it as any blur does (MEASURED).
recommendation.writes: Writes the global setting "theme" only, with one of the seven ids. It goes through the sdpi global store (useGlobalSettings("theme", onChange, null)), which merges the field into the whole global document and saves it, so readingLinks, source, pollIntervalMs, text and accent settings and unknown future fields ride along (MEASURED: all kept). It writes on a click on an unchecked chip, and on a non-repeat Arrow, Home or End press that lands on a different chip. It never writes the key's or dial's "theme" (MEASURED 0 key writes, including on an explicit key). It writes nothing on panel open, Change or reveal, focus, Tab, fold or unfold, render, a themes push, an echo, a right click, or a click on the already-checked chip (the display-checked resolved chip included), and nothing for an unknown stored value until a pick. No debounce, because pagehide saves never land, so a delayed write can be lost when another key is selected. No confirmation.

Shared defaults grows from 239.8 to 336.6 px, all inside Advanced (MEASURED, prototype). 320 px: four per row, chips about 66.5 px, whole. The prototype's chips were 59 px because of the sub-body's 24 px left inset and cut "Ultraviolet" (MEASURED), so the build pulls the gallery out to the band's inset below 200 px; the band's 65 px chips hold every name. No horizontal page overflow at any width (MEASURED 0). Targets 32 px tall, above the 24 px minimum. acceptance_tests: Change lands on the checked chip: key-configured with globals {theme:"midnight", typeAccents:"on", futureShared:{kept:true}, readingLinks:[{a:"x",b:"y"}]}. Real-click #theme-change: document.activeElement is #shared-theme .hw-theme[data-theme="midnight"] with aria-checked true and tabIndex 0; #sec-advanced and #sec-shared are open; sim.writes.length === 0 and sim.globalWrites.length === 0.

One arrow, one global write: continuing from the previous test, press ArrowRight once. sim.globalWrites.length === 1 with theme "forest"; futureShared, readingLinks and typeAccents deep-equal the fixture's; sim.writes.length === 0; after 300 ms #theme-current reads "Default (shared: Forest)" and the band's Default chip aria-label is "Default: follow the shared theme, currently Forest".
A held key picks once: focus the checked shared chip, send one ArrowRight keydown then 20 keydowns with autoRepeat:true, then keyUp. Exactly 1 new global write.

No echo needed: in one evaluate, element.click() the Paper chip and read its aria-checked synchronously; the value is "true". Then send a themes payload whose effectiveDeckTheme is the old theme: Paper stays the only checked chip and no extra write happens.
The checked chip writes nothing: click the checked shared chip. 0 new writes of either kind.

Nothing stored: key-empty with globals {} (run after a fixture that set void). The resolved theme's chip is checked and holds the Tab stop; opening writes 0 of either kind; clicking that chip writes 0.

Unknown stored value: key-configured with globals {theme:"neon"}. No shared chip checked; only Void has tabIndex 0; #shared-theme-help is shown with the text: This version does not know the stored theme "neon". Keys and dials set to Default draw Void until you pick one. 0 writes. Clicking Forest gives exactly one global write "forest" and the help hides.

An explicit key is untouched: key-custom-dim (theme ember). #theme-change is visibility hidden and cannot take focus. Picking Paper in the shared gallery gives a global write "paper", sim.writes.length === 0, sim.settings.theme === "ember", and #theme-current reads "Ember (set on this key)".
Dial parity: repeat the Change-landing and one-arrow tests on dial-configured (sensor-dial.html) with the same results.
Defined order: the shared chips' data-theme sequence is exactly void, graphite, ultraviolet, midnight, forest, ember, paper, although the sim sorts payload keys.

Accessibility tree: #shared-theme has role radiogroup and name "Shared theme"; each chip has role radio, name "<Name> shared theme" and a checked state that matches aria-checked; #theme-gallery keeps name "Theme" with 8 chips named as today.

Names whole: at widths 373, 320, 299, 240 (1.5x), 200 and 160 (3x), every #shared-theme .hw-theme-value has scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 0.5; there are 4 columns at 300 px and wider and 2 below; documentElement horizontal overflow is 0.
Panel opens write nothing: opening key-configured, key-empty, key-custom-dim, key-inherited, key-missing and dial-configured writes 0 settings and 0 global settings.

Folded band: fold #sec-theme on a Default key, then pick Ember in the shared gallery. #theme-mini .hw-theme-face background equals Ember's bg after the themes push, the fold row stays folded, and the only write is one global.

Arm meets chip: arm Replace shared settings (one press), then click a shared chip. The button returns to "Replace shared settings" with data-armed false, exactly 1 global write (the chip's), and no reload.
No right click behavior: a right-button press and release on any band or shared chip writes 0 of either kind and checks nothing new; no element with role menu appears.
Old selector gone: document.querySelector("select#shared-theme") is null; document.querySelector('.hw-theme[data-theme="ember"]') is inside #theme-gallery.
must_not: No contextmenu, auxclick, long-press or Shift+F10 behavior on any chip, and no menu widget.
No scope switch or mode on the band's gallery, and no promote link on the theme line; the band's gallery only ever writes the key's or dial's theme.
Never write the key's theme from the shared gallery or from Change, and never write the global theme from the band.
Never call setGlobalSettings({ theme }) with a partial document; merge through the sdpi global store.
Do not wait for didReceiveGlobalSettings to move the check (the app does not echo a panel's own write; the sim does).
Do not let reveal() land on the first chip; land on the group's Tab stop.
Do not let an auto-repeat keydown pick or write.
No confirmation or arming on a shared pick, and no debounce or timer on the write.
No Default chip in the shared gallery.
Do not keep the old select (hidden or not) as a second writer for the global theme.
Do not order chips by the themes object's keys; use themeOrder.
Do not change the band: chips, dashed Default with link mark, the fold row and its folded chip, the theme line, Change's words, and Change hidden on an explicit pick.
Store no UI state (localStorage or key settings) for the shared gallery; opening a panel writes nothing.
No em dashes and no "Use for all" or "all keys" claims on controls.
Do not drive the Stream Deck app or HWiNFO to verify; the right-click question stays open and this design does not depend on it.
